title: Is π^π^π^π an Integer? A Topological Attack
problem: Determine if N = π^(π^(π^π)) (right-associated) is an integer
approach: Geometrize iterated exponentiation via nested Poincaré spheres, extract integer invariants via intersection theory/counting, discretize for point-cloud fractional-part estimation
theoretical_framework: Nested Poincaré spheres (S²) with radii parametrized by topological charge ℓ
Hamilton encoder / WuBu nesting for iterative structure
Exponential map on Lie algebras for geometrizing a^b = e^{b ln a}
Intersection theory / Lefschetz fixed-point / Euler characteristic for integer invariants
Persistent homology on point clouds for fractional part estimation

computational_stack.sampling: Monte Carlo / quasi-Monte Carlo on Poincaré spheres

references: Baker's theorem on linear forms in logarithms
Persistent homology for point cloud invariants

results.conclusion: N = π^π^π^π is NOT an integer (fractional part ≠ 0)
